transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally got me to come in is people keep telling me I’m not really listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and I’m trying, I really am, but then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said and I have to ask them to repeat it. It’s been causing some problems, and I’m not trying to be rude or anything.

Can you tell me a bit more about those moments when you miss what people are saying? Are you getting distracted by other thoughts or things around you, or do you just zone out without really knowing why?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just ignoring people, because I’m really not trying to. It’s more like they’ll be talking right to me—like my supervisor explaining something, or my wife telling me something—and I think I’m following, but then a minute later I realize I only got maybe half of it.

Then I have to ask, “Sorry, can you say that again?” which… you know, doesn’t look great. I’m not always sure if it’s because my mind went somewhere else or I just kind of missed it. It just happens, if that makes sense.

When you find yourself missing parts of what someone is saying, does it feel like your attention is pulled away by other thoughts, or is it more like you’re trying to focus but just can’t seem to keep up with what’s being said?

I think it’s more like I’m trying to focus, but I don’t seem to hold onto all of it. Like, they’re talking right to me—my supervisor or my wife—and I’ll feel like I’m listening, but then a minute later I realize I only caught part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which I know probably sounds bad… I’m not meaning to, I promise.
When you're trying to listen, do you find it hard to keep your attention focused on what the person is saying from start to finish?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m not making an effort, because I am trying to listen. But if someone’s talking for more than a little bit—like my supervisor giving instructions, or my wife telling me something—I’ll think I’m following, and then suddenly I realize I only caught part of it.

So then I have to ask them to repeat it, and I feel bad because it probably comes across like I don’t care, but that’s not really it. I just… don’t seem to stay with it the whole way through, if that makes sense.
Outside of conversations, do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks like reading, working on a project, or following through with instructions?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I guess with some things, maybe, but I don’t know if I’ve really paid attention to it outside of when people are talking to me.

Like reading or projects… I don’t do a ton of reading, honestly, and at work I usually just try to keep moving and do what I’m supposed to do. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure, you know? Could you maybe say what you mean by “hard to stay focused”?
When you're reading something or working on a task that requires a bit of focus, like following instructions or finishing a project, do you find it hard to stay on track or do you lose focus easily?

I guess I’m still not totally sure. I don’t read much, so I don’t really have a good example there. With instructions, if someone shows me or I can just get started, I usually try to keep myself on track.

I mean, I probably have moments where I have to look back or ask again, but I don’t know if that’s more than anybody else. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is if I’m not sure. Does that answer what you’re asking?
When you’re working on tasks that require some focus, like reading something or following step-by-step instructions, do you find it hard to stay focused or do you lose track of what you're doing?

I’m honestly not sure. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to agree. I think if it’s something step-by-step, I can usually keep going as long as I’m doing it with my hands or I can check what comes next.

Reading is harder for me to judge because I don’t really sit and read much. I mean, I might have to look back at instructions sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s me losing focus or just making sure I’m doing it right. Does that make sense?
When you're working on tasks that need you to pay attention, like following instructions or doing something step by step, do you find yourself getting distracted or losing focus before you finish?

I… I don’t know that I’d say I get distracted before I finish, not exactly. If I’m doing something hands-on and I know the steps, I usually just keep at it.

There might be times I have to stop and check what I’m supposed to do next, or I kind of lose my place for a second, but I’m not sure if that counts as losing focus. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t finish things, because I can, most of the time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you're trying to focus on something, like following instructions or working on a task, do you find that your mind starts to wander or that you have thoughts unrelated to what you're doing?

I don’t know… I can’t say I’ve really noticed my mind wandering like that. I mean, everybody has random thoughts pop in, right? But when I’m doing a task, especially if I’m actually working on something, I’m usually just trying to get through it and do it right.

Maybe it happens sometimes and I don’t catch it, but I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Is that kind of what you’re asking?
Do you find it hard to organize tasks or keep track of multiple steps when working on something?

I’m not really sure. I mean, if there are a bunch of steps, I usually try to just take them one at a time. I don’t know that I’d say I’m “bad” at organizing it, exactly.

Sometimes I’ll look back or ask what comes next, but I kind of feel like that’s normal if there’s a lot going on. Are you meaning like forgetting the order, or more like not knowing where to start?
When you're doing something that takes a while to finish, like a project or a multi-step task, do you find it hard to stay focused on it the whole time?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. If it takes a while, I might get a little… I don’t know, tired of it, or I’ll want to get it done faster, but I usually try to stay with it.

I don’t want to say I can’t focus the whole time, because that sounds worse than I mean. It depends on the task, I guess. If it’s clear what I’m supposed to do, I can usually keep going. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you often find it hard to plan or organize the steps needed to complete a task, even if it's something you've done before?

I’m not sure… I don’t really think of it as “planning,” I guess. If it’s something I’ve done before, I usually just kind of know the routine and go through it.

Maybe if there are a lot of pieces, I’ll pause and think, “Okay, what’s next,” but I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I can’t do it. I can usually get it done. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you're trying to listen to someone or focus on a task, do you notice your own thoughts distracting you or pulling your attention away?

Yeah… I guess that is part of why I came in, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m ignoring people on purpose, because I’m really not.

But my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only got maybe half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, and I can tell it frustrates them. I don’t know if that’s my thoughts pulling me away exactly, but something happens where I’m not fully taking it in. Does that make sense?
